text:
Alex Kim: FYI - large customer reported sudden billing spike + auth errors after a regional failover around 13:02 UTC. Latency jumped and we see 401s.
Maya Patel: which customer / account id?
Alex Kim: acct_42 (internal ticket #18742). They were pinned to eu-west-1, failed over to us-east-1. Billing shows token costs routed to us-east-1 for many requests that should have stayed eu-west-1.
Jules Rivera: that's the one on Dedicated, right? they have reserved capacity in eu. :worried:
Support Bot: Ticket 18742 created, severity: P2 -> escalating to eng if customer impact persists.
Nate Ortiz: Any repro yet? Can we reproduce locally or with a curl to the gateway?
Alex Kim: I have a quick repro. When failover happens, the gateway seems to rewrite the host/region headers. Curl below shows we get 401 on the forwarded request but our auth service expects original region prefix.
```bash
curl -v -H "Host: api.redwood.example" -H "X-Client-Region: eu-west-1" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  https://gateway.redwood.example/v1/generate
# Response: 401 Unauthorized
# Gateway forwarded Host -> api.redwood.example.us-east-1.internal
```
Emily Chen: hmm, that forwarded host looks wrong. Envoy L7 should not append region suffix to :authority for internal routing. That could break our auth token validation (we validate based on service domain + region tag).
Maya Patel: can you paste a snippet of the gateway/Envoy request log (just the matched route details)?
Alex Kim: paste of envoy access log (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-15T13:02:12Z] "POST /v1/generate" 401 - via="unknown" virtual_host="api.redwood.example.us-east-1" route_name="route-failover-2026-03-15"
```
Nate Ortiz: Route name indicates the new failover route. Looks like route-failover config rewrites virtual_host to include target region. That rewrite probably bleeds into :authority header when proxying upstream.
Maya Patel: if upstream sees a different host it may pick a different tenant config or billing profile. That explains the cross-region billing. Bad.
Jules Rivera: customer complaining that tokens charged at higher single-region rates in us-east-1. We need interim mitigation.
Emily Chen: short-term mitigation: 1) revert the recent route-failover change for all routes used by Dedicated customers 2) add a header passthrough config so we don't rewrite :authority when proxying to auth service 3) pin this customer's session to eu-west-1 until fixed.
Nate Ortiz: I'll open an incident (INC-5734) and make the rollback change now. Can someone verify counterfactual traces after rollback?
Alex Kim: repro steps I've documented below — can you follow and confirm after rollback?

Repro steps:
1) Send a normal request with Host: api.redwood.example and X-Client-Region: eu-west-1
2) Simulate failover by toggling region weight to prefer us-east-1 (admin route call)
3) Observe gateway/Envoy access log for virtual_host and :authority being rewritten
4) Upstream auth returns 401 because host mismatch -> client retries -> routed to us-east-1 billing

Observed artifacts: access log virtual_host shows appended region, upstream request Host header contains region suffix, customer billing lines show token consumption in us-east-1 pool.

Maya Patel: thanks Alex. After rollback I'll run the repro flow and attach traces.
Support Bot: Incident INC-5734 created, pager notified: eng-runtime, eng-platform.
Emily Chen: long-term fix ideas: avoid mutating :authority for upstream proxying at route level. Use a separate header (X-Target-Region) for routing decisions and keep original Host intact. Also add unit tests for header preservation in route failover logic.
Nate Ortiz: assigning this to Maya (eng-runtime) and Emily (eng-platform) for the patch. I'll coordinate the rollback now.
Maya Patel: working on the revert PR, will push a canary in 5m and run Alex's repro. tagging @Emily for validation.
Alex Kim: confirmed after canary rollback: latency dropped back to ~120ms and 401s disappeared for the sample requests. Billing shows no further cross-region tokens for the test account.
Jules Rivera: I'll update the customer and pause automatic billing dispute escalation until we have full root cause and timeline.
Emily Chen: follow-ups: - postmortem on route-failover config change - add e2e for header preservation - add alert for sudden cross-region billing spikes (delta on region token distribution)
Nate Ortiz: noted. Closing interim incident once we have the PR merged to main with tests. Good catch, team. :thumbsup:
